system.name: EmbodiedBench
system.one_liner: Benchmark of 1,128 tasks in four environments and six capability subsets for evaluating vision-driven MLLM embodied agents at high and low action levels.

content.variant_note: a header chaining action formats, the wordmark and evaluated model logos over two framed galleries: four environments grouped by action level and six capability cards, each with a simulator image and an instruction
content.argues: EmbodiedBench covers both high-level semantic and low-level atomic-action tasks and tests six separate agent capabilities with targeted instruction subsets.
content.subject: A header with the two action formats, the wordmark and MLLM logos, then four environment groups by action level and six capability cards with simulator scenes and instructions.

lessons.what_to_learn: Sell a benchmark's two design axes as two tab-titled frames under a header that names the action formats, the wordmark and the evaluated models; fill each frame with equal cards (scene image plus instruction bubble) and mark the words that make each instruction test its capability in red.
lessons.suits: Benchmark papers for agents where a task is an image plus an instruction and the contribution is breadth along two axes such as action levels and capabilities.

evidence: Two key features of our benchmark: various action levels and capability-oriented evaluation.
ranging from high-level semantic tasks (e.g., household) to low-level tasks involving atomic actions
six meticulously curated subsets evaluating essential agent capabilities

summary: EmbodiedBench is a benchmark of 1,128 tasks in four environments for vision-driven embodied agents built on multimodal LLMs. Figure 1 is a gallery-style overview. A header chains the hierarchical action formats (JSON high-level actions versus a 7-D low-level vector), the EmbodiedBench wordmark and the evaluated models (logos of OpenAI, Gemini and Qwen). Below, the left frame groups four environments by action level, EB-ALFRED and EB-Habitat (high-level household, blue), EB-Navigation and EB-Manipulation (low-level, pink), each with paired simulator images and its instruction. The right frame has six green-headed capability cards, each pairing a scene with a grey speech bubble whose key words are red: base, spatial awareness, common sense, visual appearance, complex instruction and long horizon.
summary_zh: EmbodiedBench 是评测多模态大模型具身智能体的基准。图 1 顶部串起分层动作格式、标志与模型徽标；左框按动作层级分组展示四个环境，右框用六张绿色标题卡片展示六种能力，气泡中的关键词标红。
notes: No body paragraph mentions the figure; roles come from the caption, the abstract and the drawing. The prior's contribution-mosaic is kept as the second kind. The meaning of the brain icons next to the instructions is not stated. The red '(cup)' at the end of the common-sense instruction reveals the hidden target object. The pairing of the six card names with the abstract's capability list is read from the wording.
